status.next_up: Cutting the cloud, so a finished report is a file here rather than a page on the internet.

blocks.label: The real win
blocks.text: A report stops being a picture of the work and becomes the work — the same list, read and changed from one screen.

content.label: The work, in order
content.lead: Five steps. Each one is useful on its own if you stop after it.

rows.title: Stand up the shared project
rows.note: Done. Our own copy of the board screen is a project in its own right and the report tools live in it; the racing game keeps a pointer and nothing else.

rows.title: Cut the cloud
rows.note: A finished report lands as a file in that project. How it looks, what it must contain and every gate on it carry over untouched.

rows.title: The work list fills the report
rows.note: The checklist, what is happening now and what is next stop being typed by hand and start being read from the work list.

rows.title: A button on every card, and a tab for all of them
rows.note: The report opens from the card it belongs to, in whichever project that card lives.

rows.title: Buttons that act
rows.note: Answering a question or overriding a decision changes the work list as you press it, and shows you what it did.

rows: One more project to keep alive

rows.pill: Small, and it earns it back

rows: Keeping our copy of the board screen current with theirs
Building that screen needs tools this machine does not use today
A report can no longer be sent by link on its own

rows.pill: Dropped, you do not need it

rows: Every other project gets reports without doing anything
How a report looks, what it must contain, its gates

blocks.label: The one thing that can bite
blocks.text: Their board screen is someone else's project and still moving. Our addition stays small on purpose, so an update is a re-apply rather than a rewrite.

decisions.title: The report tools stay exactly as they are
decisions.why: Only where the finished page lands changes. The look, the shape and every gate carry over.

decisions.title: The checklist is the work list, never a copy of it
decisions.why: A number that can drift is a number you cannot trust.

decisions.title: A standing chore is never a checklist item
decisions.why: It can never be ticked, so it holds the bar short forever. Chores live on the work list. This retires the one open box on the blueprint page.

decisions.title: Our copy of the board screen stays thin
decisions.why: It shows reports and lists them, nothing more. Every rule about what a report is stays in our own code.

decisions.title: One report page per piece of work, named by its card
decisions.why: Same page for the life of the work, same as today.

decisions.title: Nothing already published is moved
decisions.why: Existing links keep working until the work they track lands.

decisions.title: Answering on the page writes to the work list
decisions.why: Only possible once the page is local. It shows you what it wrote, and nothing is written silently.

decisions.title: A report never leaves this machine
decisions.why: You said sharing does not matter, so nothing is built for it.

decisions.title: A report belongs to one card and opens from it
decisions.why: The card is the address. No link to keep, no list to search.

decisions.title: A report is written for you and nobody else
decisions.why: Agents read the card. Nothing goes on a report to help them do their job.

decisions.title: We keep our own copy of the board screen
decisions.why: A button on a card cannot exist without it. Override this if you would rather have the report in a second window.

decisions.title: A card with no report shows no button
decisions.why: Most cards will never have one. A button that does nothing is worse than no button.

decisions.title: Everything lives in one shared project of its own
decisions.why: The board screen, the report tools and the reports are one project, outside every product. I first had it living inside the racing game; that was wrong, and it would have kept reports from every other project you work on.

decisions.title: The racing game keeps a pointer and nothing else
decisions.why: No report code, no report files. Whatever it needs, it asks the shared project for.

decisions.title: A report is filed under its project and its card
decisions.why: One place holds every project's reports, and a card in any of them opens its own.

next.if_nothing: Reports keep going to the cloud, stay stuck to the racing game, and the checklist stays hand-typed — so it can keep disagreeing with the work list.
